title: Indie game dev Mike Houser builds an AI RPG 3x bigger than game Skyrim that's entirely procedural without assets. Are assets over?
author: sharkymcstevenson2
selftext:
He breaks down his process here:

[https://x.com/M\_\_Houser/status/2120253236309569696](https://x.com/M__Houser/status/2120253236309569696)

comments.author: Valdaraak
comments.body:
Homeboy, you *didn't even read what you posted*. He says quite clearly there are 3D models involved. The game has assets.

I also got a laugh out of him saying "everything you see and hear is code and 3D models". Yea, that's typically what a game is made out of. Only thing he cut out was audio assets.

comments.author: JustANerd420
comments.body: Please learn about things you post before you post them. You cannot make a game without assets. Assets are just computer code for one thing, telling its shape, size, color, etc.

replies.author: sharkymcstevenson2
replies.body:
I think the point is you wont need assets anymore, you can just get the output in pure code

  
You're right an asset is code, but it's just different because you dont have to rig etc

replies.body: You are sadly mistaken. Because I see nothing BUT assets in that image. The dragon, the player, the world objects, hell even the UI is a damn asset.

comments.author: TheReservedList
comments.body: I'm sure that entire space is great fun and filled with interesting content. As a professional dev I want to be on your guys side sometimes but... Jesus Christ this is clueless.

replies.body: because?

replies.author: Kosh_Ascadian
replies.body:
Because "2x the size of skyrim" is meaningless.

So the map is twice as big? Ok... how many different biomes does it have, towns, villages, special locations, inns, caves etc? How varied and interesting are they? How many quests, storylines, interesting NPC interactions etc etc.

I can make a game that is 20x the size of Skyrim in 5 minutes without AI. That means nothing. Main question is how much actual gameplay and interesting engaging content is there. For skryim theres like 100+ hours. For these things its usually 3+ minutes

comments.author: R_dva
comments.body:
Open geometry, look at the bridge. UV seams. On the  object didn't even try to hide its repetitiveness.The scale of objects is incorrect. I am sure there 0 thinking about optimization and modularity 

 And this is despite the fact that he used 3D generators, meaning he didn’t have to understood the shapes and scales himself. And still got weird scales .

Beginner-level animations that start two weeks ago to learn. I learned animation myself, so I know what I'm talking about. Of all the things, the 3D assets are the worst part. This example is bad to say  the assets is over

comments.author: monchikun
comments.body: Nothing is over. We have to see AI as an expansion of what is possible and not something that removes choice. Creativity requires intention. Someone can intend to build a guitar with hand tools (i tried and my old hands got wrecked) or power tools. An artisan will likely be able to charge significantly more for the "story" they tell about the guitar they built with hand tools and years of experience.
